554:
a. Authority, Name. This ordinance is adopted by the Board of Commissioners of Glynn County pursuant to Article IX, Section II, Paragraph I of the Constitution of Georgia (1983) and shall be referred to as the "Glynn County Noise Abatement Ordinance."
b. Findings. The Board of Commissioners of Glynn County has determined that noise is a major source of environmental pollution which represents a threat to the serenity and quality of life in Glynn County and that noise exposure may be a cause of adverse physiological and psychological effects as well as economic loss. It is the intention of this ordinance to limit noise in housing areas and other noise sensitive urban areas located in the unincorporated area of Glynn County, excluding Jekyll Island and the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center.
555:
The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this ordinance, unless otherwise specifically stated.
Construction shall mean any site preparation assembly, erection, substantial repair, alteration or similar action, for or on public or private rights-of-way, structures, utilities or real property.
Consumer Fireworks means any small fireworks devices containing restricted amounts of pyrotechnic composition, designed primarily to produce visible or audible effects by combustion, that comply with the construction, chemical composition, and labeling regulations of the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission as provided for in Parts 1500 and 1507 of Title 16 of the Code of Federal Regulations, the United States Department of Transportation as provided for in Part 172 of Title 49 of the Code of Federal Regulations, and the American Pyrotechnics Association as provided for in the 2001 American Pyrotechnics Association Standard 87-1, and additionally shall mean Roman candles.
Emergency shall mean any occurrence or set of circumstances involving actual or imminent physical or psychological trauma or property damage which demands immediate action.
Emergency Work is work made necessary to restore property to a safe condition following a public calamity or work required to protect persons or property from an imminent exposure to danger.
Fireworks means any combustible or explosive composition or any substance or combination of substances or article prepared for the purpose of producing a visible or audible effect by combustion, explosion, deflagration, or detonation, including blank cartridges, firecrackers, torpedos, skyrockets, bombs, sparklers, and other combustibles and explosives of like construction, as well as articles containing any explosive or flammable compound and tablets and other devices containing an explosive substance.
Industrial District shall mean a Basic Industrial District, Limited Industrial, or a General Industrial District as defined in the Zoning Ordinance of Glynn County.
Mechanical Sound-making Device shall mean any radio receiving device, television, stereo, musical instrument, phonograph sound amplifier or other machines or devices for the producing, reproducing or amplifying of sound and/or noise.
Motor Vehicle shall have the same meaning as O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1; which includes every vehicle which is self-propelled other than an electric personal assistive mobility device (EPAMD).
Noise shall mean any sound which disturbs humans or which causes or tends to cause an adverse psychological or physiological effect on humans.
Person shall mean any individual, partnership, firm or corporation, or any combination of one or more of them.
Plainly Audible shall mean any sound emanating from the specific sound-producing sources set forth herein which can be heard from the distances set forth herein, using the following sound measurement standards: Measurement shall be by the auditory senses of a person standing at a distance no less than the required minimum distance from the source of the sound. For music and other noise, words and phrases need not be discernible. For music and other noise, bass reverberations are included.
Plainly Audible within an adjoining residential dwelling shall mean any sound emanating from the specific sound-producing sources set forth herein which can be heard inside a residential dwelling at the distances set forth herein, using the following sound measurement standards: Measurement shall be by the auditory senses of a person standing within any living area of a residential dwelling at a distance of at least five feet from the exterior wall of the residential dwelling with all exterior doors and windows closed. For music and other noise, words and phrases need not be discernible. For music and other noise, bass reverberations are included.
Public Right-of-Way shall mean any street, avenue, highway, lane or similar place which is owned or controlled by a governmental entity.
Public Space shall mean any real property including any structure thereon which is owned or controlled by a governmental entity.
Real Property Boundary shall mean an imaginary line along the ground surface, and its vertical extension, which separates the real property owned by one person from that owned by another person, but not including intra building real property divisions.
Times shall mean Eastern Standard Time or Daylight Savings Time as observed in the State of Georgia.
Zoning Districts shall mean those districts established by the Glynn County Zoning Ordinance.

2. The use of domestic power tools or equipment as set forth in Section 2-9-53(e) of this ordinance.

560: It shall be unlawful for any person to own, possess or harbor a barking dog, or any animal or fowl which howls, barks, growls, cries, yelps, whines or emits audible sounds that are unreasonably loud or disturbing and which are of such character, intensity and duration as to disturb the peace and quiet of the neighborhood. For the purposes of this Section, "barking dog" shall mean a dog that barks, bays, cries, howls, yelps, whines or makes any other noise continuously and/or incessantly for a period of five minutes or barks intermittently for ten minutes or more to the disturbance of any person at any time of day or night regardless of whether the dog is physically situated in or upon private property; provided, however, that a dog shall not be deemed a "barking dog" for purposes of this ordinance, if at the time the dog is barking or making any other noise, a person is trespassing or threatening to trespass upon private property in or upon which the dog is situated or close proximity thereto, or for any other legitimate cause which teased or provoked the dog.
561:
(a) Variance Permit. A variance permit to cause or create a noise at sound levels which would otherwise be in violation of this ordinance may be granted by the Chief of Police if:
1. Additional time is necessary for the applicant to alter or modify the activity in order to comply with the provisions of this ordinance; or
2. The activity, operation or noise source will be of a temporary duration and cannot be done in a manner that would comply with the provisions of this ordinance; or
3. No reasonable alternative is available to the applicant.
(b) Conditions. Any permit granted pursuant to this Section shall contain therein all conditions placed upon holder of said permit as condition to the permit being granted, including but not limited to the effective date, time of day, location, sound level limit or equipment limitation. Application for such a permit shall be made in writing in such form as is acceptable to Glynn County through the office of the Chief of Police.
562:
(a) The Chief of Police shall implement, administer and enforce the provisions of this ordinance and shall issue orders requiring the abatement of all violations and the revocation of permits issued.
(b) Any person aggrieved by a decision or order rendered by the Chief of Police, after exhausting all administrative remedies, shall have the right to appeal to the Magistrate Court of Glynn County.
(c) Each and every day a violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense. Each and every violation of this ordinance, including separate violations on the same day, shall be deemed a separate offense.
(d) Any person in violation of this ordinance, upon conviction, shall be guilty of an ordinance violation punishable by a warning for the first offense and thereafter punishable by a fine of at least $100.00, but not to exceed $1,000.00; or by imprisonment of at least 24 hours, not to exceed 60 days, or both. Any person who violates this ordinance may be subject to immediate arrest. The imposition of a penalty under the provisions of this Section shall not prevent the revocation of any permit issued pursuant to this ordinance.

565: A scrambler is an electronic piece of equipment designed for dissecting the transmitting voice into parts so as to require a receiver capable of restructuring the bits of voice into an intelligible arrangement of words easily deciphered.
566: It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized person, business, or agency to purchase and use a scrambler monitor that is compatible with the scramblers and radios used by police calls and transmissions by the county police department.
567: It shall be unlawful for any person, business or agency to sell a scrambler of the above type to any person, business or other government agency without a signed agreement between the party and the county police department.
568: It shall be unlawful for any person, business or agency to alter, build or change any other radio device in such a manner as to enable any person to receive or transmit the police calls of the county police department that are being sent or received by a scrambler device.
569: The intent and purpose of Sections 2-10-1 through 2-10-4 is to enable the county police department to give orders and direct activities involving the combating of crime with the same assurance that the public has to a private telephone conversation without fear of eavesdropping.
571:
A. Hours and Conditions of Curfew. It shall be unlawful for any person under the age of 18 years of age (hereafter called minors) to be or remain upon any street, alley, park or other public property in Glynn County, Georgia except the public road, sidewalk or right-of-way immediately adjacent to the minor's domicile or on any private property without the express consent of the owner or person entitled to possession thereof (if different than the owner) between the hours of 12:00 p.m. midnight to 5:00 a.m. except that the following conditions shall excuse any such presence:
1. The minor is accompanied by his or her parent or guardian;
2. The minor is going to or from or engaged in his or her lawful employment; or
3. The minor is going immediately to or from or engaged in any event sponsored by any school or church.
B. Procedures. When any minor is believed by a peace officer to be in violation of this ordinance, he shall issue a juvenile complaint returnable to the Glynn County Juvenile Court. If the minor is 17 years of age, the officer shall issue a citation for violation of an ordinance which shall be returnable to the Magistrate Court of Glynn County, Georgia. The minor shall be detained and an attempt shall be made to contact the minor's parent or guardian. Such minor shall be released to the parent or legal guardian or referred to the Juvenile Court for disposition if under 16 years of age or taken to the Glynn County Detention Facility if 17 years old.
In every instance of a suspected violation of this ordinance by a minor, inquiry shall be made as to whether the parent(s) or natural guardian(s) of said child have also violated this ordinance.
C. Violations. Any minor willfully violating this ordinance shall be punished for a misdemeanor. Any parent or legal guardian who knowingly and willfully encourages, permits, causes, abets, connives, aids or by omission suffers a child to violate this ordinance shall be punished for a misdemeanor.
D. Effective Date. This ordinance shall be effective on the 7 th day of July, 1994.
